catalogue.note: Mara 1.0 Send, the agency design, 375×800 at real size: no scaling, every number is the file’s. Built static and for show: overlaps, collisions and off-grid values are reproduced as Figma renders them, nothing is tidied. Auto-layout frames are flex with Figma’s direction, gap, padding and alignment, and each box carries the size Figma resolved (all element boxes land within 0.25px of Figma’s). No frame chrome: the frame’s own 16px corners are left off. Send to, Description, Send from, Amount to send, with the Android keyboard over the form. The keyboard block starts at y 475 while the form runs to 512: it covers the lower 21px of “Swipe to send” and the bottom of the amount card, as in the file. The header starts at y 44, 4px inside the 48-high Android status bar, which is 374 wide in a 375 frame. Keyboard digits are live Roboto 400; the status bar and keyboard icons are Figma’s export. The sunglasses emoji that ends the description is in the text but Figma’s export draws nothing for it: kept, invisible. This frame alone carries a 1px #DDDDDD outline and a 0 4 80 shadow: frame chrome, left off; the diff leaves the 1px ring out. Figma’s untouched export (535×960, shadow included) is source/figma-export.png; source/figma.png is that export cut to the frame. Type is live Satoshi from the files on this Mac, embedded whole. Satoshi has no ₦ (U+20A6): each naira sign is Figma’s own outline of the glyph, inline, 0.572em wide. Icons and shapes are Figma’s SVG export of each node, unchanged. Figma rounds every text baseline to the nearest pixel and Chrome floors it; where the two differ (12, 11, 19, 32 and 33px type) the line carries a 1px offset worked out from Satoshi’s own metrics, so glyphs sit on Figma’s rows. What is left in the diff is glyph and curve antialiasing; flat fills match exactly.
